entries.query: Senior Java developer with Spring Framework, JPA/Hibernate, and PostgreSQL experience for an enterprise backend role.
entries.notes: Targets the Red Ocean role explicitly — Java 8 + Spring + JPA/Hibernate + Postgres. context/approach/impact carry the stack and production-defect-fix story. lessons is reflective and intentionally left out — recall@k punishes adding it only if the retriever doesn't return it. Single-achievement query.

entries.query: Quantitative researcher with options pricing theory, implied volatility surface construction, and SciPy/NumPy numerical methods.
entries.notes: Squarely the SPY volatility-surface project. Approach holds the numerical-methods detail (Newton iteration, no-arbitrage smoothing if present); impact holds the Coding Jesus feature. Single-achievement.

entries.query: LLM agent engineer building autonomous loops that iterate on their own outputs — Karpathy-style autoresearch, browser automation, agentic workflows.
entries.notes: IMC Prosperity 4 is the only achievement framed around an agentic loop. Approach is where the Karpathy-pattern adaptation lives; impact carries the PnL and the reverse-engineered submission API. Single-achievement.

entries.query: Applied ML engineer experienced with Kaggle-style competitions, gradient boosting, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization with Optuna, and feature engineering for regression problems.
entries.notes: Car-price DSC PJATK competition: XGBoost + Optuna + CatBoostEncoder, 7th of 30+ teams. Approach holds the Optuna search detail; impact has the rank + RMSE. Single-achievement.

entries.query: Full-stack engineer for a hackathon-style sprint: FastAPI backend, Angular/TypeScript frontend, end-to-end shipping under time pressure.
entries.notes: HackYeah 2025: FastAPI + Angular full stack, 24h delivery, Jury 4.3/5. Approach explains the architecture; impact the score + one-command bootstrap. Single-achievement.

entries.query: Python machine-learning engineer with hands-on PyTorch neural-network work and scikit-learn / boosting experience.
entries.notes: Cross-cutting Python+PyTorch+ML hits multiple achievements: bus-punctuality (PyTorch NN reimplementation), engineering thesis (XGBoost/LightGBM time-series), car-price (XGBoost competition), and DSC PJATK membership which umbrellas Numerai PyTorch submissions. Approach sections carry the modelling detail.

entries.query: Backend engineer with REST API design experience across production and prototype systems.
entries.notes: REST API design appears in three achievements: Red Ocean (production REST + Spring), HackYeah (FastAPI design), JMI flagship (FastAPI ingest endpoint). Approach is the natural section for design choices.

entries.query: Data engineer who has built pipelines on PostgreSQL with schema migrations and structured logging.
entries.notes: Postgres + pipeline + migrations is the JMI flagship; Red Ocean also runs on PostgreSQL but as a Spring/Hibernate app. Cross-cutting but skewed to JMI.

entries.query: Quantitative finance projects — options, derivatives, trading strategies, financial time-series modelling.
entries.notes: Volatility surface (options), engineering thesis (BTC time series), IMC Prosperity (trading). Quantfolio is also quant-adjacent but deliberately not included — it's a portfolio simulator in Java without a quant-modelling angle. Operator should reconsider if Quantfolio context belongs.

entries.query: Junior Java developer with object-oriented design experience — Spring, threads, design patterns.
entries.notes: Three Java achievements: Red Ocean (production Spring), Quantfolio (JavaFX + design patterns), Railway (multithreaded + Dijkstra). Approach carries the design choices in each.

entries.query: Programista Java backend z doświadczeniem w Spring Framework, JPA/Hibernate i bazach danych PostgreSQL.
entries.notes: Polish translation of the single-java-backend query; same relevance set. Tests worktree A's dual-embedding Polish-routing experiment — if multilingual-e5 routes correctly, recall should match the English version; English-only BGE should degrade on this query.

entries.query: Inżynier uczenia maszynowego z doświadczeniem w PyTorch, sieciach neuronowych i reimplementacji modeli z publikacji naukowych.
entries.notes: Polish ML query — bus-punctuality is the arXiv reimplementation, engineering thesis is the second ML project. Same dual-embedding test as pl-java-spring-backend.

entries.query: Junior backend developer Python z FastAPI, projektowaniem REST API i pracą z bazami danych.
entries.notes: Polish FastAPI/Python backend query — HackYeah (FastAPI + SQLite under time pressure) and JMI (FastAPI ingest + Postgres). Tests multilingual routing on a softer, less-keyword-dense query.

entries.query: Smart engineer who learns fast and ships things end-to-end.
entries.notes: Edge case: deliberately vague phrasing. 'Learns fast' and 'ships end-to-end' are reflective claims that live in `## What I learned` sections, not technical sections. Most retrievers will struggle — this query exists to surface whether per-section chunking lets `lessons` chunks rank when the query is reflective rather than technical. Operator should RECONSIDER the relevance set: every `lessons` could be argued in. I picked the four where the operator's actual learning narrative most directly matches the query frame; the rest are borderline.

Edge case: 'trading bot' is genuinely ambiguous across IMC (live agentic trading), engineering thesis (BTC signal prediction — not strictly a bot but adjacent), and volatility surface (analytical, not a bot — but a hiring manager skimming might count it). Quantfolio is deliberately excluded — it's a simulator, not a bot. Operator should RECONSIDER whether volatility-surface::context belongs in the relevant set.
